newsitem.title: GERMANY: MAN Roland declines 96/97 earnings forecast.
newsitem.headline: MAN Roland declines 96/97 earnings forecast.

text.p: German printing machinery manufacturer MAN Roland AG on Thursday declined to give an earnings forecast for the current 1996/97 business year after saying it narrowed its loss in the year ended June 30.

The subsidiary of engineering group MAN AG reported that its group net loss narrowed to 81 million marks ($52.7 million) in 1995/96 compared with 145.7 million in the year-earlier period, while group sales rose to 2.36 billion marks from 2.0 billion.
Management board chairman Peter Bruett told a news conference that sales were likely to stay unchanged in the current year.
While the company's rotary printing press business presented no problems, its sheet printing press activities urgently need orders, Bruett said.

Bruett predicted that incoming orders would rise in the current business year amid rising worldwide capital equipment spending. But he added that orders had increased only gradually in the first quarter of 1996/1997.
